## Application of the natural decay
This section simulates the decay process. Samples have been classified based on the occurrence of MST markers, but the decay rate of these markers can vary due to factors like temperature, predation, sedimentation, adsorption, and other biological or physical processes. These factors affect the survival or presence of the marker in the matrix. By determining the decay rate, the previous occurrence of markers after a specific time can be predicted. It is assumed that the inactivation rate is constant, following a linear trend, determined by the t90 value of the MST marker.

The steps are:
1. **Specify Time Period**: The user specifies the time period for simulation, using the same time units as the t90 values (hours, days, weeks, etc.).
2. **Calculate Occurrence**: The program calculates the increase in occurrence using the t90 values of the markers. This simulation applies only to quantitative variables.
3. **Save Modified Values**: The modified values are saved in a spreadsheet, which can be edited by the user.

If the user already knows the t90 values and has done the calculations, they can skip this step and proceed with the classification process. Ichnaea can use a previously trained module.

The program asks if any modifications have been made to the data file. It will wait for a response before proceeding. If modifications are confirmed, the user is prompted to upload the modified data file.

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Check if the user wants to make corrections based on the previously selected T90 values
if (tolower(t90_amendment) == 'y') {
  
  # Display a message dialog box to inform the user about the upcoming corrections and predictions
  svDialogs::dlg_message('In the next step, the user will be prompted to enter the desired time span for applying natural decay. A file will then be generated with corrections based on the t90 values and saved as a data file. Please specify the desired spreadsheet format. If any MST marker depends on another, ensure the data file is verified and corrected accordingly. These changes can be uploaded later. To continue, press "Enter" or click "OK".')$res
  
  # Display a message dialog box to select the t90 time.
  svDialogs::dlg_message('Please indicate the time for natural decay in the same units as the t90 values. A linear model will be used to amend the classification dataset. To continue, press "Enter" or click "OK".')$res
  
 # Input of the t90.time  
  repeat {
    user_input <- svDialogs::dlgInput('Please indicate the time.', password = TRUE)$res
    
    # Validate the input
    if (!is.na(as.numeric(user_input)) && as.numeric(user_input)>0 ) {
      t90.time <- as.numeric(user_input)
      svDialogs::dlg_message(paste(t90.time, ' has been selected as a decayment time. To continue, please press the "Enter" key or click the "OK" button.'))$res 
      selected.dilution.fold<-1
      break
    } else {svDialogs::dlg_message('That is an invalid value. Please enter a valid value')$res}
  }
  
  # T90 adjustment
  # Create a temporary copy of the data to classify
   names(t90s) -> variables  
   toclassify -> toclassify.temp
    
    # Adjust the values based on the t90 correction formula
    for (j in 1:length(variables)) {toclassify.temp[[variables[j]]] <- toclassify[[variables[j]]] / 10^(-as.numeric(t90.time) / t90s[,j])}

  # Display a message dialog explaining the preference for preserving the data derived from the data modified by the t90s

    svDialogs::dlg_message('Do you want to save the data derived from the t90 amendments? This step is crucial if you plan to make further modifications, such as adjusting the ratio between different MST markers. To continue, press "Enter" or click "OK".')$res

# If the user indicates that the data should be saved, proceed with the following steps
  repeat {
    svDialogs::dlgInput('Please indicate whether you wish to save the file in the Excel (1), Calc (2), CSV (3), Stata (4) or SPSS (5) spreadsheet format (1 to 5).', password = TRUE)$res->doyouwant
    if (doyouwant %in% c('1', '2', '3', '4', '5')) {
      break
    } else {
      svDialogs::dlg_message('Please enter a valid response. To continue, please press the "Enter" key or click the "OK" button.')$res
    }
  }  
  
 # Save the data in the selected format and display a confirmation message
  if (doyouwant=='1' ){
    file_path <- 'MST markers with t90 amendments.xlsx'
    save_data(toclassify.temp, file_path)
    svDialogs::dlg_message('The data file has been generated with the name: "MST markers with t90 amendments.xlsx". To continue, please press the "Enter" key or click the "OK" button.')$res
  }
  
  if (doyouwant=='2' ){
    file_path <- 'MST markers with t90 amendments.ods'
    save_data(toclassify.temp, file_path)
    svDialogs::dlg_message('The data file has been generated with the name: "MST markers with t90 amendments.ods". To continue, please press the "Enter" key or click the "OK" button.')$res
  }
  
  if (doyouwant=='3' ){
    file_path <- 'MST markers with t90 amendments.csv'
    save_data(toclassify.temp, file_path)
    svDialogs::dlg_message('The data file has been generated with the name: "MST markers with t90 amendments.csv". To continue, please press the "Enter" key or click the "OK" button.')$res
  }  
  
  if (doyouwant=='4' ){
    file_path <- 'MST markers with t90 amendments.dta'
    save_data(toclassify.temp, file_path)
    svDialogs::dlg_message('The data file has been generated with the name: "MST markers with t90 amendments.dta". To continue, please press the "Enter" key or click the "OK" button.')$res
  }    
  
  if (doyouwant=='5' ){
    file_path <- 'MST markers with t90 amendments.sav'
    save_data(toclassify.temp, file_path)
    svDialogs::dlg_message('The data file has been generated with the name: "MST markers with t90 amendments.sav". To continue, please press the "Enter" key or click the "OK" button.')$res
  }


# Display a message dialog explaining the preference to reintroduce the augmented data simulation with changes
svDialogs::dlg_message('The subsequent query concerns the necessity of modifying the data ammended with the natural decay. When utilising a CSV file, please be sure to remove the column containing the row numbers if required. To proceed, please press the "Enter" key or click the "OK" button.')$res


# Display an input dialog asking for changes in the file containing the modifications fo t90 data

repeat {
svDialogs::dlgInput('Before proceeding, the user must indicate whether modifications to the dataset with T90 amendments are required, or if a file containing the changes is already available. If neither is the case, data classification will continue using the previously generated augmented dataset. The user is asked to confirm whether any changes are desired. (y/n)?', password = TRUE)$res->doyouwant

 # Check if the user input is valid (either 'y', 'Y', 'n', or 'N')
  if (doyouwant %in% c('y', 'Y', 'n', 'N')) {
    break
  } else {
    # Prompt the user to enter a valid response if the input is invalid
    svDialogs::dlg_message('Please enter a valid response. To continue, please press the "Enter" key or click the "OK" button.')$res
  }
}

# Display an input dialog asking if LibreOffice Calc needs to be launched
if (tolower(doyouwant) == 'y'){
repeat {
svDialogs::dlgInput('LibreOffice can open files in CSV, Excel and Calc formats. If either LibreOffice Calc or Excel is installed on your computer, R will attempt to open one of these applications. Would you like R to try to open them. (y/n)?', password = TRUE)$res->doyouwant_calc  

 # Check if the user input is valid (either 'y', 'Y', 'n', or 'N')
  if (doyouwant_calc %in% c('y', 'Y', 'n', 'N')) {
    break
  } else {
    # Prompt the user to enter a valid response if the input is invalid

}
}

if (tolower(doyouwant) == 'y' && tolower(doyouwant_calc) == 'y') launch_spreadsheet()


# If the user indicates the file is available, proceed with the following steps
if (tolower(doyouwant) == 'y'){
  # Display a message dialog prompting the user to indicate the file containing the modified augmented file
  svDialogs::dlg_message('Please indicate the file that contains the modifications. To proceed, please press the "Enter" key or click the "OK" button.')$res
  
  # Open a file dialog for the user to select the dataset, allowing all file types
  svDialogs::dlg_open(title = "Select the dataset with the modifications", filters = svDialogs::dlg_filters[c('All'), ])$res->data
  
  # Import the selected data and convert it into a data frame
  toclassify.temp<-as.data.frame(import_data(data))
}
}
```

# Launch h2o.flow 
The following chunk launches H2O Flow. H2O Flow is a web-based interactive user interface developed by H2O.ai for working with the H2O machine learning platform. H2O Flow provides an interactive environment that functions in a manner analogous to that of a notebook, allowing multiple operations to be conducted by utilising a graphical interface. The initiation of the H2O Flow process is typically characterised by the execution of the H2O JAR file, followed by navigation to the URL http://localhost:54321.


```{r}
# Show a dialogue box with a welcome message 
svDialogs::dlg_message('H2O Flow is an interactive web interface that allows users to interact with the data and models generated in this module. 
If you need more information about H2O Flow, or if you need help using it, please visit this website: https://docs.h2o.ai/h2o/latest-stable/h2o-docs/flow.html. The datasets have been assigned clear and descriptive names to facilitate easy identification. Please note that some of the information that can be generated with H2O in this notebook has been omitted. You now have the opportunity to visualise this data. Once you have finished, please close the browser. Should you wish to access it again, please simply re-run this section. Press "Enter" or click "OK".')$res


 # Display an input dialog asking if h2o.flow should be launched
svDialogs::dlgInput('Should H2O Flow be launched (y/n)?', password = TRUE)$res->doyouwant
  
 # Check if the user input is valid (either 'y', 'Y', 'n', or 'N')
  if (doyouwant %in% c('y', 'Y', 'n', 'N')) {
    break
  } else {
    # Prompt the user to enter a valid response if the input is invalid
    svDialogs::dlg_message('Please enter a valid response. To continue, please press the "Enter" key or click the "OK" button.')$res
  }

# Initiates H2O Flow
if (tolower(doyouwant) == 'y'){h2o.flow()}
```
